newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas up on cooler forecast, stock data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas up on cooler forecast, stock data.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices regained at least 10 cents Wednesday, lifted by expectations for a hefty storage withdrawal figure in tonight's American Gas Association report and forecasts for cooler temperatures by the weekend in parts of the U.S., industry sources said.
Prices on the Louisiana Gulf Coast pipes rose by about 10 cents to about $3.40, down more than 40 cents from December indices.
At the Henry Hub, La., prices were heard as high as the high-$3.40s, but most deals were reported done in the low-$3.40s.
Temperatures are expected to dip to normal to below-normal by this weekend in the Northeast, Midwest and producing region.
Expectations for tonight's storage report have ranged anywhere from 60 to 125 billion cubic feet (bcf), with most in the 84-92 bcf range.
In the market areas, prices at the New York city-gate were steady to slightly higher in the $4.05-4.10 range.
Northeast Utilities said Wednesday almost 14,000 electricity customers were still without service in New Hampshire, Connecticut and western Massachusetts following last Sunday's storm.
In the Midcontinent, where a cold front is expected to arrive Saturday, prices were up at least 15 cents to the $3.33-3.38 range.
Chicago city-gate was quoted anywhere from the low-$3.50s early to the mid-$3.60s late.
In west Texas, Permian gas prices climbed about 10 cents to the mid-$3.20s.
At the southern California border, traders reported closing deals in the mid-$3.40s, also up about 10 cents. Cooler temperatures are also expected to arrive to the western U.S. early next week.
